title: For rational 1 < k < c < k squared, SAT has no eventually successful nonuniform refuter of size n to c against co-nondeterministic circuits of size n to k
author: Lijie Chen; Jiatu Li; Igor C. Oliveira
work: On the Unprovability of Circuit Size Bounds in Intuitionistic $\mathsf{S}^1_2$
source_version: LMCS volume 21 issue 3 article 26 (2025), DOI 10.46298/lmcs-21(3:26)2025; official published PDF header: Logical Methods in Computer Science Volume 21, Issue 3, 2025, pp. 26:1–26:20 https://lmcs.episciences.org/ Submitted Apr. 22, 2024 Published Sep. 10, 2025; acquired 2026-10-01 UTC

contexts.role: Exact SAT/refuter/circuit definitions, complete supporting Claim3.3 and original AB09 reference; supporting material is uncounted.

difficulty_reason: A refuter output need not reveal the truth of its SAT instance efficiently, so a single use of the refuter does not yield the desired contradiction. The proof recursively packages the complement of a longer instance into a smaller-input circuit, applies refuters across a shrinking sequence of lengths, and resolves the final instance using a hardcoded truth table. It coordinates the opposing input-size and refuter-size constraints using c < k squared, controlling all stages and the final table so that the constructed deciding circuit is itself small enough to be refuted.
